records.name: Alfonso L. Herrera
records.bio: Herrera was a Mexican biologist and naturalist whose institutional work belongs to the succession history of the Mexico City Blaschka collection. He is included where museum reorganisation and scientific administration affect how the surviving objects can be traced.

records.name: Rev. Henry H. Higgins
records.bio: Higgins had organised Liverpool’s invertebrate collections and chaired its Museum Sub-Committee. The 1887 workshop dispatch names a Higgins as recipient; contextual identification with Henry H. Higgins is strong but remains qualified because the surviving workshop text is OCR-corrupted.
records.open: The OCR-corrupted recipient in the 1887 Liverpool dispatch is strongly contextualised as Higgins, but the identification remains qualified.

records.name: Frederick Wollaston Hutton
records.bio: Hutton, a zoologist and museum curator in New Zealand, appears in correspondence concerning Blaschka models and comparative collections. His records help connect museum-side selection and ordering to the wider Ward and Australasian network.

records.name: Stephen Koob
records.bio: Koob’s work connects modern glass conservation directly to object biography. Corning conserved the Tufts models recovered from loan custody, and Vassar separately records an arrangement with him to repair and restore its Blaschka invertebrates.

records.name: E. Ray Lankester
records.bio: Lankester was a zoologist and university professor associated with the UCL teaching collection. The backend preserves a distinct 1890 Lankester catalogue and provenance layer, making him an important bridge between teaching practice, collection formation and surviving models.

records.name: Archibald Liversidge
records.bio: Liversidge was a chemist, university scientist and Australian Museum trustee whose correspondence and institutional work intersect the procurement network for scientific teaching collections. The project tracks him as a museum- and university-side intermediary rather than as a Blaschka dealer.

records.name: Godefroy Lunel
records.bio: Lunel was the first director of Geneva’s natural-history museum and is named as the recipient in the 1888 Blaschka acquisition and shipment history. His record anchors the person-level side of an otherwise institutional transaction.

records.name: Madho Singh II of Jaipur
records.bio: Madho Singh II was the ruler of Jaipur and the royal patron in the institutional setting of the Jeypore and Albert Hall Museum collections. His record represents the patronage and museum-building context around the 1886–1887 Blaschka order rather than a claim that he personally selected individual models.

records.name: Pietro Marchi
records.bio: The Florence evidence identifies Marchi as the architect of a systematic teaching collection assembled through multiple purchases. He selected catalogue models and built a local sequence that eventually numbered 118 objects; the evidence does not require that he personally made every payment or received every shipment.
